symptoms: You will see small black spots on older leaves first.
These spots grow larger and show a bullseye pattern of rings in the center.
The leaf tissue around the spots often turns yellow.
Spots can also appear on stems and may wrap around the plant near the soil.
In severe cases, the disease kills much of the plant foliage.
favourable_conditions: The disease likes warm weather with rain and high humidity.
prevention: Always use healthy seed tubers that are free from disease.
Choose potato varieties that are known to resist this disease.
Keep the field clean by removing and destroying all old plant parts after harvest.
practices: Check your plants regularly for signs of spots.
Remove and destroy any parts of the plant that show signs of the disease.
Keep the field clean to stop the spread of spores.
